# Setup Notes — Phase 1 (repo discovery)

Recorded 2026-10-26 by Claude Code. Read-only discovery; nothing was changed in the repo except this file.

## Stack

- **Language:** TypeScript (strict), some JS. Not Go, so the Go-to-UML mapping note does not apply.
- **Framework:** Next.js 14 (App Router in `apps/web/app/`, plus Pages-style modules), tRPC, Prisma/PostgreSQL, NextAuth, Tailwind. Yarn 4.12 (via Corepack) + Turbo monorepo. Node v24 verified.

## How commands are run on this machine (from `students.md`)

`students.md` is the team's Windows setup guide, verified on Windows 11. It overrides the generic commands in `AGENTS.md` where they differ.

- **Shell: Git Bash, not PowerShell.** Every repo command uses POSIX inline env vars (`TZ=UTC ...`), which PowerShell and cmd.exe can't parse. Skills must run them through the Bash tool.
- **Unit tests (Vitest, about 2 min):**
  - All: `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC yarn test`
  - One file: `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC yarn vitest run <path>`
  - The `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=""` prefix is required. `.env` sets `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1` for E2E, and that makes 7 unit tests fail by design (SSRF localhost-blocking bypass, feature rollout forced to 100%).
  - **Windows baseline: 4049 passed, 58 skipped.** Two files fail on Windows only, because of `\` path separators: `apps/web/test/lib/next-config.test.ts` and `apps/web/test/lib/pagesAndRewritePaths.test.ts`. Ignore them; they pass on CI.
  - **The test count has grown since `students.md` was written (2026-07-16); there are many more tests now.** Don't compare pass/fail totals against 4049/58. Compare a branch's results with `main`'s results on the same machine instead.
- **E2E (Playwright).** The user runs these themselves (see memory). Skills only propose the commands:
  - Don't run the suite against `yarn dev`; it hangs. Use a production build.
  - Playwright can't auto-start the server on Windows, so start it manually in Git Bash:
    ```bash
    # Terminal 1
    export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"
    yarn build
    yarn workspace @calcom/web copy-app-store-static
    NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn workspace @calcom/web start -p 3000
    # Terminal 2
    yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed
    PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn playwright test --project=@calcom/web --workers=4
    ```
  - Single spec while developing: `PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 yarn e2e apps/web/playwright/<file>.e2e.ts`
  - **Windows baseline: 243 passed, 3 failed, 27 skipped.** Known failures: `icons.e2e.ts` (no win32 screenshot baseline) and 2 reschedule tests in `booking-seats.e2e.ts` (flaky; rerun individually).
- **Build:** `export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"` first. Then `yarn build` (`turbo run build --filter=@calcom/web...`).
  - The first run may fail with a Biome error on `sprite.svg` (a CRLF/LF artifact). Run it again; the second run passes.
  - It also runs `prisma migrate deploy` against `DATABASE_URL` (issue #12). Use `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1 yarn build` when that matters.
- **Type check:** `yarn type-check:ci --force` is broken on this machine (`spawn tsc ENOENT`; see memory). Use `yarn turbo run type-check --filter=<package> --force`.
- **Lint/format:** Biome (`biome.json`): `yarn biome check --write <paths>`; `yarn lint` runs via turbo.
  - **Pre-existing errors (verified 2026-10-28):** many files already fail `biome check` on `main`. For example, `AvailabilitySettings.tsx` has `assist/source/organizeImports` and `format` errors in `main`'s own version. Running `--write` on such a file rewrites far more than your change and inflates the diff.
  - **Line endings:** `core.autocrlf=true`, so checked-out files are CRLF; CI (Linux) sees LF.
  - **Use `node .claude/course/scripts/biome-compare.mjs <files>`** to compare. It runs Biome on the LF version of the branch copy and of `origin/main`'s copy (via stdin, so files aren't touched) and labels each problem *NEW* or *pre-existing*. Only fix NEW problems.
  - `--diagnostic-level=error` hides the many `nursery` warnings and infos that already exist in the codebase.
  - Note: `biome check --stdin-file-path` without `--write` just echoes the input. Add `--write` to get the fixed output (still printed only, not written to disk).
  - Yarn 4 has no `-s` flag.
- **Database and dev server:**
  - Docker Postgres on port 5450: `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-up`, then `db-deploy` / `db-seed` / `db-reset`.
  - Mailhog on 8025/1025; app on http://localhost:3000.
  - `packages/prisma/.env` must be a real copy of the root `.env` (the symlink is broken on Windows). Re-copy it after editing `.env`.
  - Seeded logins: `pro@example.com`/`pro`, `free@example.com`/`free`, `admin@example.com`/`ADMINadmin2022!`. Useful for manual verification steps in PR descriptions.

## CI (GitHub Actions)

- `.github/workflows/pr.yml` runs on `pull_request_target` and fans out to lint, type-check, unit tests, API v2 unit tests, security audit, builds, e2e.
- Code PRs (e.g. #110) actually run **Linters, Type Checks, Tests / Unit, Tests / API v2 Unit**. E2E and production builds are skipped (no `ready-for-e2e` label).
- **Security Audit fails** on PR #110 and makes the `required` check fail. This looks pre-existing (not caused by that PR); `/preflight` should report the individual checks rather than only `required`.
- Docs-only PRs skip nearly every job.
- `Validate PR title` enforces conventional-commit titles.

# Implementation plan: #117, PR 1 (AC1–AC3: choose and save the days)

Written by `/dev-implement 117` on 2026-10-29. Sources: `spec.md` (on the issue, teammate-approved by kojoshuay), `design.md`, `impact.md`. PR 2 (AC4–AC5: helper, series generation, ICS/links, first-slot check) gets its own plan after PR 1.

## Before Step 1 (user)
- The branch is **17 commits behind `origin/main`** (`git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD` → `17 0`). Those commits touch files this plan uses: `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/types.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/types.ts`, `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`, and add `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.test.tsx` (the pattern for Step 4's component test). The branch has no commits of its own yet, so a fast-forward is enough.
- `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` shows as modified, but `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` is empty: line endings only. Don't commit it.

## PR split
PR 1 as one PR is 11–12 files (limit 10, AGENTS.md). Proposed stacked split, each safe to merge on its own:
- **PR 1a = Steps 1–2 (data and saving):** 5 files, about 130 lines. Nothing writes the new fields until PR 1b, so merging it changes no behaviour for users.
- **PR 1b = Steps 3–4 (UI):** 6 files, about 230 lines. Once merged, saved days reach series generation with the UTC weekday bug until PR 2 lands (see `impact.md` §7), so merge PR 2 before the release.

## Steps

### Step 1 — Types and Zod schema (PR 1a) — AC2 (server side), AC3
- **Goal:** the rule can carry `byweekday` (integers 0–6, `rrule` numbering, 0 = Monday) and `wkst` (integer 0–6); an existing-but-empty `byweekday` is rejected; a rule without them still parses.
- **Files:**
  - `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:129-136`: `byweekday?: number[]`, `wkst?: number`.
  - `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:239-248`: `byweekday: z.array(z.number().int().min(0).max(6)).min(1, "recurring_select_at_least_one_day").optional()`, `wkst: z.number().int().min(0).max(6).optional()`. The integer range also guards `rrule` against values that would make it throw or hang (design M1).
  - Maybe `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/types.ts:278-285` (`RecurringEventInput`), only if type-check needs it.
- **Tests:** `packages/prisma/zod-utils.test.ts` (existing): keeps `byweekday`/`wkst`; rejects `[]`, `7`, `-1`, `1.5`, `"TU"`; a rule without them parses unchanged.
- **Size:** about 10 source + 40 test lines.

### Step 2 — Save the fields in the update handler (PR 1a) — AC3

Arguments given to this skill: "117 - do step 1" (the issue number). If missing, ask and stop.

The user must be able to explain every line (course). So you work in **small, approved steps** and stop after each one. No code edits are pre-approved, so the user sees every edit.

### Step 0 — Preconditions (check, then report)
- **Spec and design:** `.claude/work/issue-<N>/spec.md` and `design.md` should exist, or equivalent sections on the issue (`gh issue view <N> --json body,comments`). If either is missing, **stop** and suggest `/plan-spec` or `/plan-design`. Continue only if the user explicitly says to.
- **Teammate spec review:** if no teammate has commented to approve the spec, warn that the course wants it before coding. The user decides whether to go on.
- **Branch:** if the current branch is `main` or unrelated to the issue, give the commands for the user to run, each explained:
  ```bash
  git fetch origin
  git switch main && git pull origin main          # start from the latest main
  git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-<slug>              # or fix/issue-<N>-<slug> for a bug
  ```
  If `main` has uncommitted changes, point that out first: they would come along to the new branch.

### Step 1 — Plan (then stop)
Write `.claude/work/issue-<N>/plan.md`. It holds an ordered list of small steps, each with:
- its goal;
- the files to touch (`file:line` for edits to existing code);
- the tests to add or update;
- which acceptance criteria it serves.

Each step should be committable on its own. Keep the whole change under the PR limit (500 code lines and 10 code files, AGENTS.md). If it won't fit, plan a stacked split now.

Follow `AGENTS.md` and `agents/rules/`:
- `select` not `include` in Prisma;
- `import type` for type imports;
- no barrel imports;
- `ErrorWithCode` outside tRPC routers;
- translations in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`;
- no `as any`;
- comments only for "why".

Ask before schema changes, new dependencies, or changes that span several packages (AGENTS.md).

Ask: **"Approve this plan (or edit it)?"** and stop.

### Step 2 — One step per turn
When the user says to do the next step (or a specific one):
1. Make only that step's edits, code and tests together. Match the surrounding code's style.
2. Then **stop and report**, in this order:
   - **What changed:** each file, with `file:line` and a short snippet of the key lines.
   - **Why.**
   - **Assumptions made.**
   - **How it relates to existing code:** callers and callees, with `file:line`.
   - **What could go wrong:** edge cases and risks.
   - **Tests added or updated,** and what each one proves.
   - **Checks:** run the relevant parts of `/dev-checks` for the touched files (`node .claude/course/scripts/checks-plan.mjs` gives the commands) and report the results. NEW vs pre-existing problems are told apart as in `/dev-checks`.
   - **Files to commit for this step,** plus a **draft commit message** (conventional commit, e.g. `feat(scope): … (#<N>)`), for the user to commit:
     ```bash
     git add <files>
     git commit -m "<message>"
     ```
   - **Running diff size:** `node .claude/course/scripts/pr-facts.mjs`, giving code lines and files so far against the 500 / 10 limit.
   - **A reminder** to check the VS Code Problems panel and to try the change in the running app. The user runs the dev server and E2E.
3. Update `plan.md`: mark the step done and note any change to the plan.

Never go on to the next step in the same turn. If a step turns out bigger or different than planned, stop and re-plan with the user.

### When all steps are done
Suggest `/dev-checks` for a full run, `/dev-explain "last change"` if the user wants a walkthrough, then `/pr-draft <N>`.

Step 1 is done: the recurring rule can now carry the weekdays and the week start, and an empty day list is rejected. The 29 tests in `zod-utils.test.ts` pass, and both type-checks are clean.

## What changed
**`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:247-252`**: two optional fields in the `recurringEventType` schema.
```ts
// rrule weekday numbers (0 = Monday). Integers only: other values make rrule throw or loop forever.
byweekday: z
  .array(z.number().int().min(0).max(6))
  .min(1, { message: "Select at least one day" })
  .optional(),
wkst: z.number().int().min(0).max(6).optional(),
```
**`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:136-137`**: `byweekday?: number[] | undefined;` and `wkst?: number | undefined;` added to `RecurringEvent`.

**`packages/prisma/zod-utils.test.ts`**: the import now includes `recurringEventType`, and there's a new `describe("recurringEventType")` block at the end.

## Why
- **AC3:** without these fields, Zod strips the days on save and again when the event is read back.
- **AC2:** an empty list is rejected by the server.
- **Design M1:** numbers in the `rrule` scheme, 0 = Monday.

## Assumptions
- `.optional()` means "no list", which stands for the old behaviour (your decision A). Only an empty list that exists is an error.
- The Zod message is plain English, like the other messages in `zod-utils.ts` (e.g. `:257` "Invalid ISO Date"). Hosts will see the translated message under the row, added in Step 5, not this one.

## How it connects
- The same schema validates the tRPC update input (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/types.ts:141`, `recurringEventType.nullable().optional()`, Confirmed). It also parses the stored rule when it's read back, through `parseRecurringEvent` in `packages/lib/isRecurringEvent.ts` (Confirmed in `impact.md`).
- The handler (`update.handler.ts:244-252`) still copies the fields one by one, so **nothing is saved yet**. That's Step 2.
- `RecurringEvent` is used in about 200 files. Both new fields are optional, so existing code doesn't need to change.

## What could go wrong
- **Every rule read back now goes through the stricter check.** A stored rule with a bad `byweekday` would fail to parse. None can exist yet, because nothing has written the field before.
- **Code that builds its own rules** (e.g. API v2 2024-04-15, `update-event-type.input.ts:258`) is unaffected: it sends neither field.
- **`RecurringEventInput`** (`packages/features/eventtypes/lib/types.ts:280`) wasn't touched. If a later type-check of `@calcom/features` complains, it gets the same two fields.

import type { RecurringEvent } from "@calcom/types/Calendar";

export function isRecurringEvent(obj: unknown): obj is RecurringEvent {
  const parsed = recurringEventSchema.safeParse(obj);

  return parsed.success;
}

export function parseRecurringEvent(obj: unknown): RecurringEvent | null {
  let recurringEvent: RecurringEvent | null = null;

  if (isRecurringEvent(obj)) recurringEvent = obj;

  return recurringEvent;
}

```typescript
import type { z } from "zod";

import { Frequency, type recurringEventType } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";
import type { RecurringEvent } from "@calcom/types/Calendar";

type RecurringEventRule = NonNullable<z.infer<typeof recurringEventType>>;
type StoredWeekdayFields = Pick<RecurringEvent, "byweekday" | "tzid" | "wkst">;

/**
 * Decides which recurring rule to save when an event type is updated.
 * - Only weekly rules keep selected days: the form keeps them while the host switches to
 *   "month" or "year" so they come back on switching back, but they must not be saved, because
 *   rrule reads BYDAY on a monthly rule as "every one of those weekdays in the month".
 * - A weekly update without days (e.g. from API v2, whose recurrence input has no days) keeps
 *   the days, time zone and week start already saved, instead of silently erasing them.
 */
export function mergeRecurringEventUpdate(
  input: RecurringEventRule,
  stored: StoredWeekdayFields | null
): RecurringEventRule {
  if (input.freq !== Frequency.WEEKLY) {
    const { byweekday: _byweekday, wkst: _wkst, ...withoutWeekdays } = input;
    return withoutWeekdays;
  }

  if (input.byweekday !== undefined || !stored?.byweekday) return input;

  return {
    ...input,
    byweekday: stored.byweekday,
    tzid: input.tzid ?? stored.tzid,
    wkst: input.wkst ?? stored.wkst,
  };
}

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { Frequency } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";

import { mergeRecurringEventUpdate } from "./recurringWeekdays";

const weekly = { interval: 1, count: 8, freq: Frequency.WEEKLY };
const savedDays = { byweekday: [1, 3], tzid: "America/New_York", wkst: 6 };

describe("mergeRecurringEventUpdate", () => {
  it("saves the selected days, time zone and week start of a weekly rule", () => {
    const input = { ...weekly, ...savedDays };
    expect(mergeRecurringEventUpdate(input, null)).toEqual(input);
  });

  it("uses the new days when the host changes them", () => {
    const input = { ...weekly, byweekday: [0, 4], tzid: "Europe/London", wkst: 0 };
    expect(mergeRecurringEventUpdate(input, savedDays)).toEqual(input);
  });

  it.each([Frequency.MONTHLY, Frequency.YEARLY])("drops days and week start for frequency %s", (freq) => {
    const result = mergeRecurringEventUpdate({ ...weekly, ...savedDays, freq }, savedDays);
    expect(result).toEqual({ interval: 1, count: 8, freq, tzid: "America/New_York" });
    expect(result).not.toHaveProperty("byweekday");
    expect(result).not.toHaveProperty("wkst");
  });

  it("keeps the saved days, time zone and week start when a weekly update leaves them out", () => {
    const apiV2Update = { interval: 2, count: 10, freq: Frequency.WEEKLY };
    expect(mergeRecurringEventUpdate(apiV2Update, savedDays)).toEqual({ ...apiV2Update, ...savedDays });
  });

  it("leaves a rule saved before days existed unchanged", () => {
    expect(mergeRecurringEventUpdate(weekly, { tzid: undefined })).toEqual(weekly);
    expect(mergeRecurringEventUpdate(weekly, null)).toEqual(weekly);
  });
});

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-30 04:13:27Z)**_

Step 2 is done, using option (a). The update handler now saves the days and week start, drops them for monthly and yearly rules, and keeps the saved ones when an update leaves them out. The tests pass, and Biome and all three type-checks are clean.

## What changed
**New `packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.ts`:** a pure function that decides which rule to save.
```ts
export function mergeRecurringEventUpdate(input: RecurringEventRule, stored: StoredWeekdayFields | null) {
  if (input.freq !== Frequency.WEEKLY) {
    const { byweekday: _byweekday, wkst: _wkst, ...withoutWeekdays } = input;
    return withoutWeekdays;                                    // month/year: don't save days
  }
  if (input.byweekday !== undefined || !stored?.byweekday) return input;
  return { ...input, byweekday: stored.byweekday, tzid: input.tzid ?? stored.tzid, wkst: input.wkst ?? stored.wkst };
}
```
A short comment above it explains why each rule exists.

**`packages/trpc/.../heavy/update.handler.ts`:**
- Two imports added (`:12`, `:14`).
- `:247-250`: `const ruleToSave = mergeRecurringEventUpdate(recurringEvent, parseRecurringEvent(eventType.recurringEvent));`
- `:257-259`: `tzid`, `byweekday` and `wkst` are now taken from `ruleToSave`. The other fields are unchanged, so the existing `dstart` typo and casts stay as they were.

**New `packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.test.ts`:** 6 tests.

## Why
- **AC3:** days are saved and shown again when the host reopens the event.
- **Design C:** days are kept in the form, but not saved for month or year.
- **Decision 7:** an API v2 update doesn't erase saved days.
- **Option (a):** the logic is easy to test outside the 600-line handler.

## Assumptions
- **The stored rule is always loaded already.** `recurringEvent` is in the handler's existing `select` (`update.handler.ts:105`, Confirmed), so there's no extra query.
- **A stored rule that fails the stricter schema from Step 1 counts as no stored rule.** `parseRecurringEvent` returns `null` for it (`packages/lib/isRecurringEvent.ts:10-14`, Confirmed). Nothing has saved days before now, so no such rows exist.
- **`tzid` is kept for monthly and yearly rules.** It's an older field that API v2 2024-04-15 can set; only the two new fields are dropped.

## How it connects
- The handler only reaches this code when the input has a rule (`if (recurringEvent)`, `:246`). `null` still clears the rule (`:261-262`), and leaving the rule out still changes nothing.
- The input type is the Zod type from Step 1 (`recurringEventType`, used by the tRPC input at `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/types.ts:141`).
- `packages/lib` imports only `@calcom/prisma/zod-utils` and `@calcom/types`, which is allowed (`agents/rules/architecture-circular-dependencies.md`).
- API v2 event-type updates reach the same handler through `packages/platform/libraries/event-types.ts`. That's the decision-7 case (path found by dependents.mjs; Unverified end to end).

- **"Keep when left out" also means "can't remove days" through an update that leaves them out.** That's intended: the UI never sends an empty list (AC2 rejects it), and turning recurring off sends `null`.
- **A weekly update that leaves out days but includes a new `tzid`** keeps the stored days with the new zone. That's reasonable, but nothing sends it today.

## What changed
**`packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.ts:8-16`**
```ts
// Saved rules use rrule's numbering (0 = Monday), but Date.getDay() and the user's week-start
// setting use 0 = Sunday. Converting anywhere else risks moving every selected day by one.
export function jsDayToRRuleWeekday(jsDay: number): number {
  return (jsDay + 6) % 7;
}
export function rruleWeekdayToJsDay(rruleWeekday: number): number {
  return (rruleWeekday + 1) % 7;
}
```
**`packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.test.ts`:** a table of all 7 days, plus a `describe("weekday number conversion")` block. The import now includes both functions.

## Why
Design M1: one tested place for the `getDay()` (0 = Sunday) ↔ `rrule` (0 = Monday) mismatch you asked to note. Step 5 uses it when the host clicks a day button and to set `wkst` from the week-start setting. PR 2 uses it to check which weekday a slot falls on.

## Assumptions
- **The input is a whole number from 0 to 6.** No range check here: the saved values are already checked by the Zod schema from Step 1, and the inputs are `getDay()` values or loop indexes.
- **The user's week-start setting becomes a `getDay()`-style number** through `weekStartNum` (`packages/lib/weekstart.ts`), which is how `EventAvailabilityTab.tsx:195` uses it. Unverified that it returns 0 = Sunday; I'll confirm it in Step 5.

## What could go wrong

- **Negative or larger inputs** give wrong results (for example `jsDayToRRuleWeekday(-1)` is `-1 % 7` = `-1`). They can't happen with the inputs described above.

Step 4 is done: the Recurring tab now receives the logged-in user's time zone and start of week. Nothing visible changes yet. The real type-check (`@calcom/web`) passes. The type-check commands the checks script suggested for `@calcom/features` and `@calcom/atoms` turned out to check nothing; details under Checks.

## What changed
| File | Line | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/recurring/RecurringEventController.tsx` | `:22` | New optional prop `user?: { timeZone: string; weekStart: string };` (not used yet) |
| `packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/recurring/EventRecurringTab.tsx` | `:9`, `:22` | Takes `user` and passes it on: `user={user}` |
| `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` | `:259` | `recurring: <EventRecurringTab eventType={eventType} user={user} />` |
| `packages/platform/atoms/event-types/wrappers/EventTypePlatformWrapper.tsx` | `:283` | `user={user?.data}` on `EventRecurringTabPlatformWrapper` |

## Why
- **AC1:** the day row needs the user's start of week to order the buttons.
- **Design 2:** the browser fills `tzid` and `wkst` from the user.

## Assumptions
- **The prop's type is a plain `{ timeZone: string; weekStart: string }`, not the Prisma `User` type.** Types from the database don't belong in `packages/features` UI code (`agents/rules/data-dto-boundaries.md`, team).
- **`weekStart` is a day name such as `"Sunday"`.** `weekStartNum` turns it into 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday, and anything unknown becomes 0 (`packages/lib/weekstart.ts:5-9`, Confirmed). That answers Step 3's Unverified point.

## How it connects
- **Web:** `user` comes from `useMeQuery()` (`EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:121`) and is already passed to the Availability and Advanced tabs (`:236`, `:253`).
- **Platform:** `user?.data` is what the parent already passes to the availability wrapper (`:240`), whose prop is `Pick<User, … "timeZone" | … "weekStart">` (`EventAvailabilityTabPlatformWrapper.tsx:14`). So the shape matches (Confirmed).
- **The thin wrappers forward `user` without changes:** `EventRecurringWebWrapper` and `EventRecurringTabPlatformWrapper` spread `props`, and their props type is `Omit<RecurringEventControllerProps, "paymentEnabled">` (`EventRecurringTab.tsx:7`).

## What could go wrong
- **`user` is `undefined` while the profile loads, or when a platform app doesn't provide it.** Step 5 must handle that: Sunday-first order, and no `tzid`, which means today's UTC behaviour (design 2 consequence).
- **Platform atoms have outside users.** The prop is optional, so their code keeps compiling.

## Tests
None for this step, as planned: it only passes a value through. Step 5's component test renders the controller with `user`.

## Checks
- **Biome:**
  - `RecurringEventController.tsx` is clean.
  - The other three files have import-order and format problems that are the same on `main`. Formatting LF copies shows none of the reported lines are mine; the one formatter hit in `EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` is an unrelated `enum([...])` list.

import type { EventTypeSetup, FormValues } from "@calcom/features/eventtypes/lib/types";
import { Frequency } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";
import type { RecurringEvent } from "@calcom/types/Calendar";
import { fireEvent, render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import type { UseFormReturn } from "react-hook-form";
import { FormProvider, useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import RecurringEventController from "./RecurringEventController";

vi.mock("@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale", () => ({
  useLocale: () => ({
    t: (key: string) => key,
    i18n: { language: "en" },
  }),
}));

const newYorkMondayFirst = { timeZone: "America/New_York", weekStart: "Monday" };

let form: UseFormReturn<FormValues>;

function Harness({
  recurringEvent,
  user,
}: {
  recurringEvent: RecurringEvent | null;
  user?: { timeZone: string; weekStart: string };
}) {
  const methods = useForm<FormValues>({
    defaultValues: { recurringEvent, seatsPerTimeSlot: null, maxActiveBookingsPerBooker: null },
  });
  form = methods;
  const eventType = { recurringEvent } as unknown as EventTypeSetup;
  return (
    <FormProvider {...methods}>
      <RecurringEventController eventType={eventType} paymentEnabled={false} user={user} />
    </FormProvider>
  );
}

const weekly = { interval: 1, count: 8, freq: Frequency.WEEKLY } as RecurringEvent;

const weekdayButtons = () => within(screen.getByTestId("recurring-event-weekdays")).getAllByRole("button");
const dayButton = (name: string) => screen.getByRole("button", { name });

describe("RecurringEventController weekday row", () => {
  it("shows seven day buttons for a weekly rule, ordered from the user's start of week", () => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={weekly} user={newYorkMondayFirst} />);
    expect(weekdayButtons().map((button) => button.getAttribute("aria-label"))).toEqual([
      "Monday",
      "Tuesday",
      "Wednesday",
      "Thursday",
      "Friday",
      "Saturday",
      "Sunday",
    ]);
  });

  it("starts on Sunday when no user is given", () => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={weekly} />);
    expect(weekdayButtons()[0].getAttribute("aria-label")).toBe("Sunday");
  });

  it.each([Frequency.MONTHLY, Frequency.YEARLY])("hides the row for frequency %s", (freq) => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={{ ...weekly, freq } as RecurringEvent} user={newYorkMondayFirst} />);
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("recurring-event-weekdays")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("saves selected days as rrule numbers with the user's time zone and week start", () => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={{ ...weekly, byweekday: [] }} user={newYorkMondayFirst} />);
    fireEvent.click(dayButton("Thursday"));
    fireEvent.click(dayButton("Tuesday"));

    expect(form.getValues("recurringEvent")).toEqual({
      ...weekly,
      byweekday: [1, 3],
      tzid: "America/New_York",
      wkst: 0,
    });
    expect(dayButton("Tuesday").getAttribute("aria-pressed")).toBe("true");
    expect(dayButton("Monday").getAttribute("aria-pressed")).toBe("false");
  });

  it("saves Sunday as rrule 6 and a Sunday week start as wkst 6", () => {
    render(
      <Harness
        recurringEvent={{ ...weekly, byweekday: [] }}
        user={{ timeZone: "Europe/London", weekStart: "Sunday" }}
      />
    );
    fireEvent.click(dayButton("Sunday"));
    expect(form.getValues("recurringEvent")).toMatchObject({ byweekday: [6], wkst: 6 });
  });

  it("does not write a time zone or week start when no user is given", () => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={{ ...weekly, byweekday: [] }} />);
    fireEvent.click(dayButton("Tuesday"));
    const saved = form.getValues("recurringEvent");
    expect(saved).toMatchObject({ byweekday: [1] });
    expect(saved).not.toHaveProperty("tzid");
    expect(saved).not.toHaveProperty("wkst");
  });

  it("shows the message when the last selected day is deselected", () => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={{ ...weekly, byweekday: [1] }} user={newYorkMondayFirst} />);
    expect(screen.queryByText("recurring_select_at_least_one_day")).toBeNull();

    fireEvent.click(dayButton("Tuesday"));

    expect(form.getValues("recurringEvent")?.byweekday).toEqual([]);
    expect(screen.getByText("recurring_select_at_least_one_day")).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it("starts a newly enabled rule with an empty day list and shows the message", () => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={null} user={newYorkMondayFirst} />);
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("recurring-event-check"));

    expect(form.getValues("recurringEvent")?.byweekday).toEqual([]);
    expect(weekdayButtons().every((button) => button.getAttribute("aria-pressed") === "false")).toBe(true);
    expect(screen.getByText("recurring_select_at_least_one_day")).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it("shows no message for a rule saved before days existed", () => {
    render(<Harness recurringEvent={weekly} user={newYorkMondayFirst} />);
    expect(screen.queryByText("recurring_select_at_least_one_day")).toBeNull();
    expect(form.getValues("recurringEvent")).not.toHaveProperty("byweekday");
  });

  it("keeps the selected days in the form while the row is hidden for a monthly rule", () => {
    render(
      <Harness
        recurringEvent={{ ...weekly, freq: Frequency.MONTHLY, byweekday: [1, 3] } as RecurringEvent}
        user={newYorkMondayFirst}
      />
    );
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("recurring-event-weekdays")).toBeNull();
    expect(form.getValues("recurringEvent")?.byweekday).toEqual([1, 3]);
  });
});

Step 5 is done, and with it all of PR 1. The Recurring tab now shows the day buttons, writes the days with the user's time zone and week start, and shows a message when no day is selected. All 55 tests in the three test files pass, Biome is clean, and `@calcom/web` type-checks with 0 errors.

## What changed
**`RecurringEventController.tsx`** (+71/−1):
- **Imports:** `jsDayToRRuleWeekday`, `weekdayNames`, `weekStartNum` (`:10-12`).
- **`:73-75`:** the user's week start, the short and long day names in that order, and the host context:
  ```ts
  // Saved with the days so the booking side judges "Tuesday" by the host's clock and week.
  const hostWeekContext = user ? { tzid: user.timeZone, wkst: jsDayToRRuleWeekday(weekStart) } : {};
  ```
- **`:77-86`, `toggleWeekday`:** adds or removes the day (as an `rrule` number), keeps the list sorted, adds `tzid`/`wkst`, and writes to the form, the same way the other rows do (`setValue(..., { shouldDirty: true })`).
- **`:142`:** turning recurring on for a new rule starts with `byweekday: []` (AC1, no default).
- **`:195-237`:** the row, shown only when `freq === Frequency.WEEKLY`.
  - It has a "Repeats on" label and seven `<button type="button" aria-pressed aria-label={long name}>` toggles. Selected buttons use the same brand style as the date picker (`bg-brand-default text-brand`).
  - When `byweekday` is `[]`, it shows `<p className="text-error …">{t("recurring_select_at_least_one_day")}</p>` (AC2).
- **Optional `customClassNames.weekdaysInput`** (`container`/`label`/`button`), so platform apps can style the new row like the others. `impact.md` said new keys must be optional.

**`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:1083-1084`:** `"repeats_on": "Repeats on"` and `"recurring_select_at_least_one_day": "Select at least one day"`.

**New `RecurringEventController.test.tsx`** (144 lines): 11 tests.

## Why
- **AC1:** the row appears only for weekly, in start-of-week order, with no default.
- **AC2:** the message under the row (your choice), with the Zod rule from Step 1 as the actual rejection.
- **AC3:** the days are kept in the form when switching frequency.
- **Design 2:** `tzid`/`wkst` come from the browser.
- **M1:** `rrule` numbers, through the Step 3 helper.
- **M2:** plain toggle buttons.

## Assumptions
- **The user's zone and week start are saved when the host first clicks a day.** If the host never touches the row, an existing rule keeps whatever `tzid`/`wkst` it already has.
- **Without `user`, no `tzid`/`wkst` is written**, so the series keeps today's UTC behaviour (design 2 consequence).
- **Old rules (no `byweekday`) show all buttons unpressed and no message.** That follows your decision A.

## How it connects
- `weekStartNum` (`packages/lib/weekstart.ts:5`) gives 0 = Sunday; `jsDayToRRuleWeekday` converts it for `wkst` (`packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.ts:10`).
- `weekdayNames(locale, weekStart, format)` (`packages/lib/weekday.ts:5`) returns names starting at the week start, so button `index` is `getDay()` day `(index + weekStart) % 7`. That's the same pattern as `EventAvailabilityTab.tsx:198`.
- On save, the form value goes to the tRPC update: Zod (Step 1) rejects `[]`, and `mergeRecurringEventUpdate` (Step 2) drops days for month/year and keeps saved ones when they're left out.

## What could go wrong
- **Saving with no day selected:** the server rejects it, and the existing error toast (`EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:157-176`) also appears, alongside the message under the row. How readable that toast's text is remains Unverified. **Please check this one in the app.**
- **Button labels in other languages:** if a locale's short names are long, the row could wrap on narrow screens (`h-8 min-w-8 px-2`, `flex gap-1`).
- **`user` arrives after the first render:** buttons that are clicked before the profile loads save without `tzid`/`wkst`. That's unlikely, since the page waits for the user.
- **Not covered by a test: switching month → week through the real dropdown.** The `react-select` dropdown is awkward to drive in jsdom. The test checks that the days stay in the form while the row is hidden, and the dropdown's existing `onChange` already copies the whole rule.

## Tests: `RecurringEventController.test.tsx` (11 new)
| Test | Proves |
|---|---|
| seven buttons, Monday-first for a Monday user | AC1 order follows the setting |
| Sunday-first when no user | Safe default |
| hidden for MONTHLY / YEARLY | AC1 |
| Thursday then Tuesday → `byweekday: [1, 3]`, `tzid`, `wkst: 0`; `aria-pressed` | AC3, M1, design 2, sorted |
| Sunday → `[6]`, Sunday week start → `wkst: 6` | The `getDay()` ↔ `rrule` edge case you flagged |
| no user → no `tzid`/`wkst` | Design 2 fallback |
| deselect the last day → `[]` and the message | AC2 |
| enabling recurring → `[]`, nothing pressed, message | AC1 (no default) and AC2 |
| old rule without days → no message, no `byweekday` added | Decision A |
| monthly rule keeps days in the form while hidden | Design C |

## What does this PR do?

Closes #117

Hosts can now choose which weekdays a weekly recurring event repeats on (e.g. Tuesday and Thursday). The choice is saved with the event type and shown again when the host reopens it. This is the first of two PRs for #117: it covers AC1–AC3 (choose and save the days). Building the series on those days in the host's time zone (AC4) and the server check of the first slot (AC5) follow in a second PR; hiding unselected days on the booking page is #118.

### What changed
- **Data shape:** `recurringEventType` accepts `byweekday` (integers 0–6 in `rrule` numbering, 0 = Monday; at least one when present) and `wkst` (integer 0–6) (`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:248-253`); the `RecurringEvent` type has both as optional fields (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:136-137`). `recurringEvent` is a JSON column, so there is no migration.
- **Saving:** `update.handler.ts:249-262` passes the input rule and the stored rule to the new pure function `mergeRecurringEventUpdate` (`packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.ts:26-43`), which drops `byweekday`/`wkst` when the frequency isn't weekly, and keeps the stored days, `tzid` and `wkst` when a weekly update leaves them out (e.g. an API v2 update, whose recurrence input has no days).
- **Weekday numbering:** `jsDayToRRuleWeekday` / `rruleWeekdayToJsDay` (`packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.ts:10-16`) convert between `Date.getDay()` (0 = Sunday) and `rrule` (0 = Monday) in one tested place.
- **User passed to the tab:** `EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:259` and `EventTypePlatformWrapper.tsx:283` pass the user to `EventRecurringTab` (`EventRecurringTab.tsx:9,22`), which forwards it to the controller (`RecurringEventController.tsx:25`, optional `{ timeZone, weekStart }`).
- **Day row:** `RecurringEventController.tsx:195-237` shows seven toggle buttons (`<button type="button" aria-pressed aria-label>`) for weekly rules only, ordered from the user's start of week (`:71-73`). Clicking a day (`toggleWeekday`, `:77-86`) writes the sorted days plus `tzid` (user's time zone) and `wkst` (user's week start) to the form. A newly enabled rule starts with no days (`byweekday: []`, `:142`), and an empty list shows "Select at least one day" under the row (`:232-234`). New optional `customClassNames.weekdaysInput` (`:39-43`) for platform-atoms styling.
- **Strings:** `repeats_on`, `recurring_select_at_least_one_day` (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:1083-1084`).

### Why
A weekly recurring event could only repeat on the weekday of the first booking, so a host who holds sessions on Tuesday and Thursday couldn't offer one recurring event for both. This PR meets:
- **AC1:** the day row appears only for "week", ordered from the host's start of week, with no day preselected.
- **AC2:** an existing-but-empty day list is rejected on save (Zod) and flagged under the row; event types saved before this change have no list and save as before.
- **AC3:** the days are saved and shown again on reopen; old event types keep their behaviour; switching to month/year keeps the selection in the form but doesn't save it; an update without days keeps the saved ones.

### Why this PR is over the file limit
12 code files (AGENTS.md limit: 10), about 380 lines (limit 500). 4 of the 12 are test files, 3 are one- or two-line hand-offs of the `user` prop, and splitting would separate the saving from the UI that produces the values.

### Design
The design decisions for #117 (decisions 1 and 3 apply to the second PR):

_**User (2026-10-30 05:20:28Z)**_

Can you explain what git merge origin/main does? Does it mess with the remote main branch?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-30 05:20:38Z)**_

No. `git merge origin/main` only changes **your local branch**. It never changes `main` on GitHub.

**What the two commands do**
1. **`git fetch origin`** downloads the latest commits from GitHub and updates your local, read-only copy of the remote branch, called `origin/main`. Think of `origin/main` as a snapshot of GitHub's `main` stored on your machine. Fetching never changes your own branches or files.
2. **`git merge origin/main`** (run while you're on `feat/issue-117-weekly-recurring-events`) takes the commits in that snapshot that your branch doesn't have yet (here #116, the availability toggle) and combines them into **your branch**. Git records this as one new "merge commit" on your branch. Your files now contain your work plus main's latest changes.

**What it does not do**
- It doesn't change `main` on GitHub, or your local `main` either.
- It doesn't send anything anywhere. Only `git push` publishes, and the command I gave, `git push -u origin feat/issue-117-weekly-recurring-events`, pushes **your feature branch**, not `main`.
- `main` only changes when a teammate merges your PR on GitHub.

**Why do it before pushing**
- The PR then shows only your changes against an up-to-date `main`.
- If your work and the new commits clash, you find out and fix it locally, where you can rerun the tests, instead of in the PR.

**For your branch specifically**
The two new commits touch `common.json` at line 321, and your lines are 1083–1084, so git should combine them automatically. If it ever reports a conflict, you can resolve it, or run `git merge --abort` to go back to exactly how your branch was before the merge.

**Why merge rather than rebase**
A rebase rewrites your branch's commits on top of `main`, which means a force-push if the branch was already pushed. AGENTS.md says never to rebase or force-push shared branches. A merge only adds a commit, so it's safe.

No new feedback entries.

## Fix when you push: your branch tracks `main`
Your branch's upstream is set to `origin/main` (`branch.feat/issue-117-weekly-recurring-events.merge = refs/heads/main`). That probably happened when the branch was created from `origin/main`. It **hasn't changed anything on GitHub**, but:
- a bare `git pull` would pull `main`, and `git status` compares against `main`;
- a bare `git push` is refused, because the branch names differ.

Push with the explicit form. The `-u` also resets the upstream to your own branch:
```bash
git push -u origin feat/issue-117-weekly-recurring-events   # publish your branch AND make it track origin/feat/issue-117-… instead of main
```
Afterwards, `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u}` should print `origin/feat/issue-117-weekly-recurring-events`.

`e1cfb607b6` "feat(event-types): add test cases for recurring event" has no `(#117)`, and it's a `test:` change. That doesn't matter for CI: the PR **title** is what's checked, and squash-merging uses the title. Fixing it would mean rewriting a commit that sits behind the merge, so I'd leave it.

**Two things I noticed while gathering, outside the diagrams:**
- **PR #126 is open, but not as a draft.** AGENTS.md says to open PRs as drafts.
- **Its title, "Feat/issue 117 weekly recurring events", isn't a conventional-commit title.** CI's `Validate PR title` check will likely fail on it. Rename it to e.g. `feat(event-types): choose which weekdays a weekly recurring event repeats on (#117)`.

## How React/TypeScript maps to UML here
- Components become classes with the `<<component>>` stereotype, and hooks get `<<hook>>`.
- Props and state become attributes; functions become operations.
- Modules of plain functions become `<<module>>`, and Zod schemas become `<<schema>>`.
- "renders" and "uses" are dependency arrows.

## Class diagram (8 elements)
| Element | Kind | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EventTypeWebWrapper` | `<<component>>` | **modified** (passes `user`) | `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:121` (`useMeQuery`), `:134` (`updateMutation`), `:180` (`useEventTypeForm`), `:259` |
| `useEventTypeForm` | `<<hook>>` | existing | `packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:288` (`handleSubmit`), `:290` (`getDirtyFields`), `:412` (`onSubmit`) |
| `EventRecurringTab` | `<<component>>` | **modified** | `packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/recurring/EventRecurringTab.tsx:9,22` |
| `RecurringEventController` | `<<component>>` | **modified** | `RecurringEventController.tsx:25` (`user`), `:39-43` (`weekdaysInput`), `:55-56` (form context, `recurringEventState`), `:71-75`, `:77` (`toggleWeekday`) |
| `recurringWeekdays` | `<<module>>` | **new** | `packages/lib/recurringWeekdays.ts:10`, `:14`, `:26` |
| `RecurringEvent` / `recurringEventType` | `<<interface>>` / `<<schema>>` | **modified** (+`byweekday`, `wkst`) | `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:129-138`, `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:240-254` |
| `updateHandler` | `<<tRPC handler>>` | **modified** | `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/heavy/update.handler.ts:62`, `:98-105`, `:246-260`, `:710` |
| `parseRecurringEvent` | `<<function>>` | existing | `packages/lib/isRecurringEvent.ts:10` |

**Relationships:**
- `EventTypeWebWrapper` → *renders* → `EventRecurringTab` → *renders* → `RecurringEventController`.
- `EventTypeWebWrapper` → *uses* → `useEventTypeForm`.
- `RecurringEventController` → *uses* → `recurringWeekdays` and → *writes* → `RecurringEvent`.
- `updateHandler` → *uses* → `parseRecurringEvent` and `recurringWeekdays.mergeRecurringEventUpdate`.
- `updateHandler`'s input is validated by `recurringEventType`.

`EventTypePlatformWrapper` (`:283`, one line) gets a note rather than its own box.

## Sequence diagram
**Trigger:** the host clicks **Tuesday** in the Recurring tab, then clicks **Save**.

**Participants:** Host, `RecurringEventController`, `recurringWeekdays`, react-hook-form, `useEventTypeForm`, `EventTypeWebWrapper` (`updateMutation`), tRPC `update` (Zod input), `updateHandler`, Prisma.

**Main path:**
1. `toggleWeekday(1)` (**new**) uses `jsDayToRRuleWeekday` (**new**) to pick the button's day number, then `setValue("recurringEvent", { …, byweekday, tzid, wkst })` (**new values**).
2. Save: `handleSubmit` → `getDirtyFields` → `onSubmit` → `updateMutation.mutate` (all existing).
3. tRPC validates the input with `recurringEventType` (**modified**: rejects `[]`).
4. `updateHandler` → `prisma.eventType.findUniqueOrThrow` (selects `recurringEvent`, existing) → `parseRecurringEvent` (existing) → `mergeRecurringEventUpdate` (**new**) → `prisma.eventType.update` (existing, `:710`) → success toast.

**One `alt` block:** empty day list → Zod `BAD_REQUEST` → error toast. The inline message under the row already shows before saving.

## Annotations (3)
1. **Design 2:** `tzid`/`wkst` come from the logged-in user in the browser (note on `RecurringEventController`).
2. **M1:** stored days use `rrule` numbering (0 = Monday); `getDay()` uses 0 = Sunday, and the conversion lives in one module (note on `recurringWeekdays`).
3. **Design C + decision 7:** on save, days are dropped for month/year and kept when an update leaves them out (note on `mergeRecurringEventUpdate`).

The text is unreadable for two reasons, and a screenshot is the main one.

**1. Resolution: the screenshot captured the screen, not the diagram.**
- The class diagram is very wide, so to fit it on screen the editor zoomed out until the text was a few pixels tall. The screenshot saved it at that size: the class PNG is about 1,100 px wide for the whole diagram, which is why the member text is a blur.
- Mermaid draws diagrams as vector graphics (SVG), so an **export** renders at full size no matter how far the editor is zoomed out.

**2. Theme: it was exported in dark mode.**
- That's why the sequence diagram's green blocks have light-grey text on light green, and why the class boxes show coloured outlines but no green/yellow fill.

These PNGs also predate the `#117` legend fix, which is why the legend still stops at "…modified by".

## How to fix it
**Option A (I'd recommend it): I render the PNGs here with the Mermaid CLI.**
```bash
npx -y -p @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli mmdc -i docs/sprint2/diagrams/117-dchan01-wm-class.mmd -o docs/sprint2/diagrams/117-dchan01-wm-class.png -t default -b white -s 3
```
- `-t default` is the light theme, `-b white` gives a white background, and `-s 3` renders at 3× scale, so the text stays sharp when zoomed.
- It downloads about 150 MB (Mermaid plus a headless Chromium) the first time, which is why I need your OK.
- **The real advantage:** I can then open the PNG myself and check it, so we fix layout problems together instead of you re-exporting after every change.

**Option B: export from mermaid.live yourself, with no screenshot.**
1. Paste the `.mmd` file.
2. In the **Config** tab, set `{"theme": "default"}`.
3. Use **Actions → PNG** (or **SVG**) to download the real export.

This works too, but I can't see the result until you send it back.

## The diagrams themselves also need work
Even rendered sharply, the class diagram is badly laid out:
- **`direction LR` with long notes makes it very wide.** Switching to `direction TB` (top to bottom) and shortening the notes would make it closer to a page shape.
- **`mergeRecurringEventUpdate(input: RecurringEventRule, stored: StoredWeekdayFields | null)` is the widest line in its box.** I can shorten the parameter types in the diagram and keep the full signature in the note.
- **The green/yellow fills didn't appear.** That might just be the dark theme, or Mermaid ignoring my `cssClass` lines. With Option A, I'd see which one right away.

**Which option, A or B?** With A, I'll render, look at both PNGs, and propose the layout changes with the before and after images. Either way, the PNGs on `docs/dchan01-wm_diagrams_v2` get replaced, so the next commit on that branch updates them.
